comment: Outlets whose public RSS/Atom feeds fill the weird-news front page (/api/weird, lib/weird.js). As with the brief (data/news-sources.json) we show only the outlet's own headline, its name, the time, a link to the story and the outlet's own link-preview image: never its description, opening paragraph or article text. Every item passes the moderation rules in lib/moderation.js first. NOT YET VERIFIED: on 16 Nov 2026 every host below was refused by the build sandbox's network proxy, so feed addresses come from publisher patterns, feed directories and search-index copies (scout research). 'checked' stays null until the feed has been fetched and parsed on a Vercel preview (/api/weird?debug=1 shows each feed's status and item count). The owner should review and approve this list before launch. Guardian and NPR are left out on purpose: their feed terms are personal, non-commercial use only.
fields: name: shown as the outlet. section: the outlet's section the feed covers. home: the outlet's page we link to (also its own-site boundary for og:image reads). images: false = no picture is read or shown, and its article pages are never fetched. review: true = a higher-risk outlet; its items appear only if moderation passes, never above a regular outlet's item, at most 3 at a time. categoryHints: lower-case words found in the feed's own <category> labels -> our category. filter: when present, an item is kept only if one of its feed categories contains one of 'categories' or its URL path contains one of 'paths'. exclude: an item is dropped when its headline contains one of 'titles' (whole words, any case) or its URL path one of 'paths'. licence: what we know about the terms.

sources.name: UPI
sources.licence: Unknown: no feed reuse terms found (upi.com footer Terms of Use not read). Preview photos are often Reuters/AP/Getty wire photos: keep the images switch and takedown route ready.

sources.name: Sky News
sources.licence: Unknown (news.sky.com/info/terms-and-conditions not read). The feeds.skynews.com/feeds/rss/<section>.xml pattern is confirmed; the strange.xml filename is not.

sources.name: Atlas Obscura
sources.licence: Unknown (terms page found, not read in full). Prefer /feeds/articles over /feeds/latest, which is mostly user-submitted places.

sources.name: ScienceDaily
sources.licence: Known: feeds free for commercial and non-commercial use with ScienceDaily credited as the source (terms dated 7 Jan 2026); the outlet name is shown on every item. The terms count 'altering content or failing to display it' as a breach: ask ScienceDaily whether headline-and-link complies before launch. Images off: they are usually credited to the releasing institution.

sources.name: Mental Floss
sources.licence: Unknown (mentalfloss.com/terms-of-use not read). Shopping and deal posts are filtered out.

sources.name: Live Science
sources.licence: Unknown (Future plc terms not read). General feed, filtered to strange-news items by category or URL. Runs graphic medical case reports: the injury rule holds those.

sources.name: SoraNews24
sources.licence: Unknown (no terms page found). General feed, filtered to the weird category; crime and sexual content are held or dropped by moderation.

sources.name: Oddity Central
sources.licence: Unknown (no terms page found). High risk: rewrites other outlets' stories and runs viral private individuals, medical conditions and poverty. Images off; lower priority; review outlet.

sources.name: NDTV
sources.licence: Unknown (footer terms not read). High risk: heavy on viral clips of private people and accidents. Images off; lower priority; review outlet. The feedburner address is from memory: drop it if the preview shows it failing.
